title: Keep named-condition shortcut in the wizard, persist only functional presets
description:
REVISED 2026-08-30 after the human raised that stripping clinical vocabulary is an accessibility regression. Operating systems name these conditions in their own accessibility settings (macOS and Windows colour filters both list Protanopia/Deuteranopia/Tritanopia), and a user with a known diagnosis should not have to re-derive it by comparing swatches.

DESIGN: split clinical naming from clinical STORAGE by lifetime. Keep the condition names in the UI as a one-click shortcut; use the answer TRANSIENTLY, in memory, to select a preset; persist only the functional result from oculist-rnr.12. Nothing about the user's health is ever written to disk or synced.

Current wizard (extension/welcome.html:236-272) asks clinically AND persists the answer. Steps 1 and 3 are the clinical ones ('Do you experience color blindness?' with Deuteranopia/Protanopia/Tritanopia options; 'Do you experience eye strain').

Steps:
1. Keep the named-condition options in the wizard UI. Do NOT delete the clinical vocabulary from welcome.html. A user who knows their diagnosis keeps the direct path.
2. ADD a second entry point alongside it: a sample-comparison path for users who do not know or prefer not to say. Step 1 offers both - pick a named option, or compare rendered colour samples and choose the clearest. Both paths must reach the same set of presets.
3. Make the clinical answer TRANSIENT. welcome.js:159-167 resolves the selection; from there it must map straight to the functional preset key from oculist-rnr.12 and persist ONLY that. The condition string must never be written to chrome.storage.sync, chrome.storage.session, chrome.storage.local, localStorage, or any other sink, and must never be transmitted.
4. Audit the whole wizard path for incidental persistence of the clinical answer: intermediate wizard state, resume-after-reload state, the setupWizardCompleted flag's payload, and anything popup.js reads back. If the wizard persists partial progress, ensure the clinical selection is not part of what is stored.
5. Accept the UX consequence and handle it deliberately: because the condition is not stored, reopening settings later shows the FUNCTIONAL preset name, not 'Deuteranopia'. Make that display sensible and non-confusing (e.g. a clear preset name plus a way to re-run the picker). Do not fake persistence by stashing the condition somewhere.
6. Preserve accessibility throughout. Every option, named or sample, must be keyboard reachable, have an accessible name describing the visual result, and not rely on colour alone to be distinguishable. This wizard serves users with vision differences; the change must not degrade it for them.

Edge cases:
- Do NOT change which preset a given answer produces. Behaviour stays identical for every existing choice.
- The sample path must be genuinely usable by someone with the deficiency it serves: samples need a non-colour distinguishing cue (label, shape, or position), since a user may not discriminate the colour axis being demonstrated.
- If a sample-based step 1 needs assets that do not exist, use text descriptions of the visible result ('warmer reds', 'stronger blue-yellow separation') for that path rather than dropping it. Report what you did.
- Step 3's eye-strain wording should become preference-framed ('How much animation do you want?') since 'do you experience eye strain' is a symptom question with no diagnostic shortcut value. Steps 2 and 4 likewise: ask about the visible result.

Done-criteria:
- The named-condition shortcut still exists in the wizard UI.
- A sample/preference path exists alongside it, reaching the same presets.
- grep across ALL storage sinks confirms no clinical string is ever persisted: no condition name in chrome.storage.*, localStorage, or any transmitted payload.
- The wizard produces the same presets and the same rendering outcomes as before.
- Every option keyboard reachable with a descriptive accessible name; samples distinguishable without relying on colour.
- npm test passes at exactly 212 tests, 212 pass, 0 fail, PLUS a test asserting the clinical selection is not persisted by the wizard.

title: Convert visionProfile from clinical labels to functional preset keys, with migration
description:
HUMAN DECISION 2026-08-30: Oculist moves from the Clinical Profile row to the Functional Preset row of the CWS data-classification mapping. Persist rendering values, not condition names. Existing users get MIGRATE AND OVERWRITE.

Current state (verified):
- visionSettings (content.js:19) is ALREADY purely functional: colorPalette, customColors{matchColor,activeColor,beaconColor}, beaconSize, animationSpeed, borderStyle, textLabels, magnifier, motionSensitivity. Consumed at content.js:498-535, 3029, 3071, 3100, 3169, 3365, 4665. Leave this field alone.
- visionProfile is the ONLY clinical artifact. Values written: 'color-blind-deuteranopia', 'color-blind-protanopia', 'color-blind-tritanopia' (welcome.js:34,42,50), 'low-vision' (welcome.js:26), 'eye-strain' (welcome.js:58), 'custom' (popup.js:110,210), null (popup.js:191, welcome.js:659).
- visionProfile is LOAD-BEARING, not decorative: content.js:2873 branches on 'eye-strain'; content.js:5092 renders a display label. Both must keep working.

This bead changes the STORAGE SCHEMA and its consumers ONLY. The wizard's question wording is a separate bead (oculist-rnr.13) - do NOT reword questions here.

Steps:
1. Replace the visionProfile field with a functional key. Proposed name: displayPreset, holding functional values. Mapping, preserving current behaviour exactly:
   - 'low-vision'                -> 'high-contrast'
   - 'color-blind-deuteranopia'  -> 'rg-adjust-deut'
   - 'color-blind-protanopia'    -> 'rg-adjust-prot'
   - 'color-blind-tritanopia'    -> 'by-adjust'
   - 'eye-strain'                -> 'reduced-motion'
   - 'custom'                    -> 'custom'
   - null                        -> null
   If you find a better functional vocabulary that stays behaviour-identical and carries no clinical term, use it and say so in your report. The hard rule: NO stored value may name a medical condition.
2. Update SETTINGS_KEYS (content.js:44) and the defaults block (content.js:18).
3. Update every consumer: content.js:2873 (the eye-strain branch), content.js:5092 (the display label - it must render functional wording now, not 'Color Blind'), popup.js:110/151/191/210, welcome.js:659.
4. MIGRATION, load-bearing. On settings load, if a stored oc-settings carries the old visionProfile field, map it through the table above into the new key, WRITE the migrated settings back, and DELETE the old visionProfile field from chrome.storage.sync. After migration no clinical string may remain in storage. Put the migration where settings are first read, and make it idempotent - it must be safe to run on every load and a no-op once migrated.
5. Handle the null/absent cases: a user who never ran the wizard, and a user mid-wizard. Neither may throw.

Edge cases:
- The settings write path echoes through chrome.storage.onChanged and has self-write detection (content.js:48-60, pendingSelfWrites). A migration write MUST NOT tear down the panel or trigger an echo loop. Read that comment block before writing the migration.
- popup.js:110 and :210 set 'custom' when the user hand-edits a value; that behaviour stays.
- Do NOT change visionSettings, and do NOT change any rendering behaviour. This is a rename plus migration; the extension must look and behave identically before and after.

Done-criteria:
- grep -rniE 'deuteranopia|protanopia|tritanopia|color-blind|colorblind|eye-strain|low-vision' extension/*.js returns NOTHING outside welcome.html question text (which oculist-rnr.13 handles).
- No stored value names a medical condition.
- Migration maps old to new, writes back, deletes the old field, and is idempotent.
- Rendering behaviour is unchanged for every preset.
- npm test passes at exactly 212 tests, 212 pass, 0 fail, PLUS new tests covering the migration: each old value maps correctly, migration is idempotent, and absent/null profiles do not throw.

title: Multi-term search lists (v1.7.0)
description:
Let the user hold a list of search terms, run them against the current page, and carry
the list to the next page. One term is active at a time with the full existing beacon
treatment; the rest stay dim-highlighted. Named lists persist in sync storage.

Approved design: ../artifacts/plans/v1.7.0-2026-08-25-multi-term-lists-design.md
(from repo root: /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/plans/v1.7.0-2026-08-25-multi-term-lists-design.md)

Shape of the change:
- performSearch() splits into buildPageIndex() + findRanges(); performListSearch() runs
  the index once and findRanges per term.
- searchRanges stays the active term's ranges, so findNext/highlightActiveRange/beacons/
  viewport markers need no changes.
- Three CSS.highlights registries with explicit priorities: dim(0) < match(1) < active(2).
- Working list in chrome.storage.session (oc-worklist); saved lists in chrome.storage.sync
  one key per list (oc-list-<id>).
- No new manifest permissions.

in the popup.

title: Stop DOM-mutation rescan from scrolling the viewport back to the active match
description: Oculist's MutationObserver-driven rescan called highlightActiveRange(false), which ran element.scrollIntoView(...) and yanked the viewport back to the active match whenever the page mutated (lazy-load, infinite scroll) while the user was scrolling elsewhere. Fix: added skipScroll parameter to highlightActiveRange, passed true from rescanAfterMutation, and gated the scroll branch on !skipScroll. Interactive navigation (typing search, prev/next, replay) is unaffected.

title: fadeActiveBeacons wipes the persistent accessibility overlays, not just the transient beacon
description:
Reviewer finding during oculist-9t5, verified by execution. Pre-existing for full motion; oculist-9t5 extended its blast radius to reduced motion.

fadeActiveBeacons() (extension/content.js, called from handleScroll) fades and removes EVERY .oc-beacon element. But drawActiveOverlays() classes the persistent accessibility overlays as .oc-beacon too - the border (around :3262), the shape (:3297), the label (:3325) and the magnifier card (:3439). So the first scroll after a match wipes them all, not just the transient beacon effect.

Measured with borderStyle 'thick': full motion, before=2 after=0 - already the behaviour today. Reduced motion, before=2 after=2 before oculist-9t5, before=2 after=0 after it. So 9t5 did not create this bug, it made reduced motion consistent with full motion, which is the direction 9t5 wanted for the transient beacon and the wrong direction for these overlays.

Why it is the wrong direction: unlike the transient beacon, these overlays are positioned in DOCUMENT coordinates and track scroll correctly. They are not stale, they are not misleading, and they are the high-visibility affordance the whole product exists to provide. Fading them on scroll is pure loss, and it lands hardest on exactly the users who turned a thick border on.

FIX: the fade query is too broad. Tag the transient beacon elements distinctly - a second class such as oc-beacon-transient on what the effects draw - and have fadeActiveBeacons() select only those, leaving the persistent overlays alone. cancelBeacons() should keep clearing everything, since a new search legitimately tears the whole set down. Check every place that creates a .oc-beacon and decide per site which category it is; animateReducedMotion draws BOTH kinds (a transient glow and, under displayPreset reduced-motion, an arrows+spotlight overlay), so it needs care.

Do not simply exclude the overlays by their own class names - that is a fourth list to keep in sync with drawActiveOverlays. One positive marker on the transient elements is the maintainable version.

TEST: with borderStyle 'thick', run a search, scroll, and assert the border overlay survives while the transient beacon is gone. Cover both full and reduced motion.

title: speed_lines.test.js 'survives a scroll between capture and read' now fails: fadeActiveBeacons correctly fades/removes the beacon on real scroll, so speedLinesDone never fires
description:
test/speed_lines.test.js's 'the centre-line highlight anchor check survives a scroll between capture and read' test (around line 446) fails as a direct, correct consequence of the oculist-qii fix.

Root cause: this test does window.scrollTo(0, SCROLL_AT_CAPTURE), fires the beacon, then window.scrollTo(0, SCROLL_AT_READ) while the beacon is still live, and then waits for window.__ocTest.speedLinesDone to become true. Before oculist-qii, fadeActiveBeacons() (content.js, called from handleScroll() on every 'scroll' event) already faded and removed the .oc-beacon element ~50ms after any scroll, but it did NOT cancel the animateSpeedLines() rAF loop — the loop kept running on the orphaned, detached canvas until it reached its own natural completion (t >= 1), which is what set speedLinesDone = true. The test's "wait for speedLinesDone" only ever passed because of that leak.

oculist-qii fixed exactly this: fadeActiveBeacons() now goes through the same destroyBeacon() helper as cancelBeacons(), so it cancels container.__rafId (and any __waapiAnims) atomically with removal. After the fix, the second scrollTo() in this test genuinely fades and removes the beacon and cancels its rAF loop, so the loop never reaches its completion branch and speedLinesDone never becomes true — the test times out (15s) waiting for it.

This is not a flake and not a regression in the fix; it's an existing test whose premise (a beacon can be scrolled mid-flight and still reach natural completion) is no longer true now that scrolling correctly cancels beacons. The test's real intent, per its own name/history (oculist-viv), is to verify that the centre-line highlight's document-coordinate math stays correct across an intervening scroll — not to test whether a beacon survives a scroll.

Needs a design decision on how to restructure this test now that "scroll mid-flight" and "beacon still animating" are mutually exclusive:
- Read the anchor value at a moment before the 50ms fade-removal window closes (i.e. immediately after the second scrollTo(), before the fade timer fires), instead of waiting for speedLinesDone.
- Or add a test-only escape hatch (e.g. exposing a way to force isAutoScrolling true) so the scroll doesn't trigger fadeActiveBeacons() — mirrors real auto-scroll navigation, but changes what the test actually exercises.
- Or pick two scroll positions during which the effect legitimately completes before any scroll fires (removes the "between capture and read" scroll entirely) and cover the coordinate-math regression a different way.

Verified by running the full suite after the oculist-qii fix: 284 passing, 1 failing (this test) out of 285 total (283 baseline + 2 new oculist-qii tests). Not the known stale_mount_guard flake.

title: fadeActiveBeacons removes beacons without cancelling their rAF loop
description:
Reviewer finding during oculist-3ae. Pre-existing, affects EVERY canvas effect, and it is the root cause blocking oculist-3ae.

extension/content.js's fadeActiveBeacons() (around :4957, called from handleScroll) removes .oc-beacon elements but never cancels container.__rafId. cancelBeacons() (around :1024-1042) does cancel-then-remove; fadeActiveBeacons() only removes.

Consequence: any scroll during a live beacon detaches the container while its requestAnimationFrame loop is still scheduled. The loop keeps running against a detached canvas, and because cancelBeacons() finds its targets via document.querySelectorAll('.oc-beacon'), the detached container is permanently unreachable - nothing can ever cancel it. The loop only stops when it reaches its own completion branch.

Reproduced 2/2 with a real page.mouse.wheel mid-beacon; 0/1 without the scroll. Instrumented trace: 'fadeActiveBeacons activeBeacons=1' -> container removed at frame 23 -> loop continues 25, 26 ... 32 -> later 'cancelBeacons n=0'.

Today this is mostly wasted work on a detached canvas. It becomes a crash the moment any effect's frame loop READS a property off a hook the next run can null - which is exactly what oculist-3ae's hook reset introduces for chrono's lastChronoHueRun.hueSamples.push. See the comment on oculist-3ae for the full trace.

FIX: make fadeActiveBeacons() cancel the same way cancelBeacons() does before removing - cancelAnimationFrame(container.__rafId) and clear __waapiAnims - rather than duplicating that logic, factor out the single teardown both call. Check every other place that removes a .oc-beacon for the same omission.

TEST: scroll during a live beacon and assert the effect's frame counter stops advancing after the removal. test/chrono_tunnel.test.js's 'no frame() runs after the beacon container is removed' case (on branch wip/oculist-3ae) is the shape to copy, driven by a real scroll instead of natural completion.

BLOCKS: oculist-3ae. Fixing this first lets 3ae land with no per-push null guards.

Verify all line references against current files before acting.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
HALTED on a stop condition: the fix turns the full suite red. Work preserved on branch wip/oculist-qii (commit effccfd), NOT on the epic branch. Do not merge as-is.

THE FIX ITSELF LOOKS RIGHT and is unreviewed only because the run halted before the reviewer was dispatched. It extracts destroyBeacon(b) - cancelAnimationFrame(__rafId) + cancel every __waapiAnims entry + remove() - out of cancelBeacons(), and calls it from fadeActiveBeacons()'s existing 50ms setTimeout in place of the bare .remove(). Cancelling at removal rather than at fade start is deliberate: during the fade the beacon is still attached and so still reachable by cancelBeacons(), and cancelling at fade start would freeze the canvas mid-fade.

BLOCKER: test/speed_lines.test.js 'the centre-line highlight anchor check survives a scroll between capture and read' (around :446) now times out at 15s. Suite is 284 pass / 1 fail. See oculist-a96 for the full analysis.

Short version: that test scrolls to SCROLL_AT_CAPTURE, fires the beacon, scrolls to SCROLL_AT_READ while it is still live, then waits for window.__ocTest.speedLinesDone === true. Pre-fix, the second scroll made fadeActiveBeacons() detach the beacon but leave its rAF loop running, and the orphaned loop ran on to its natural completion branch, which is what set speedLinesDone. The wait only ever succeeded because of the bug this bead fixes. Post-fix the loop is genuinely cancelled, so speedLinesDone never fires.

The test's real intent is worth keeping: it checks that lastSpeedLinesContainerRect is captured in document coordinates, so a scroll between capture and read cannot corrupt the anchor. That assertion is still valid; only its 'wait for natural completion' mechanism is not.

NEEDS A HUMAN CALL - how should that coverage be preserved?
(A) Stop waiting for speedLinesDone. Read lastSpeedLinesHighlightY and lastSpeedLinesContainerRect right after the scroll, off the frames the test already waited for (it polls speedLinesFrameCount >= 2 before scrolling). Keeps the anchor assertion, drops the dependency on completion. Looks like the cleanest fit to me, but it does mean the test no longer exercises a full run end to end.
(B) Move the scroll to after completion. Preserves the end-to-end run but stops testing 'scroll BETWEEN capture and read', which is the whole point of the test's name.
(C) Have the test suppress the fade for its own duration (e.g. drive the scroll without a scroll event, or restore the beacon). Keeps both properties but adds test-only machinery to work around real product behaviour.

ALSO FOUND, not yet its own bead - decide whether it warrants one: drawActiveMatchLabel (around :3321) and drawActiveMatchMagnifier (around :3384) each do a bare existing.remove() to replace a previous same-id overlay while its __waapiAnims may still be running (a 250ms label fade, an up-to-470ms magnifier lift). Same omission this bead fixes, different call sites, and neither is one of the effects' own completion self-removals. They should probably go through destroyBeacon() too.

AUDIT RESULT for the record: cancelBeacons() and fadeActiveBeacons() are the only two general teardown paths and both now route through the helper. Every effect's own completion self-removal (chrono ~:2811, speedlines ~:2631, and the WAAPI effects) was reported and deliberately left alone - cancelling from those setTimeout(DUR) timers kills the legitimate final frame, as disproven by execution during oculist-3ae. Those belong to oculist-3ae and oculist-ws4.

TEST NOTE worth keeping: the two new tests needed document.body.style.paddingBottom = '2000px' because the existing fixture pages are exactly one viewport tall, so a wheel scroll was a no-op and the tests passed for the wrong reason until that was added.

title: isOculistNode/isOculistMutation ignores text-node mutations and beacon-descendant elements, causing spurious background rescans (e.g. Cyber-Vision's readout textContent write)
description:
Found while implementing oculist-3ae. content.js's isOculistNode() (used by isOculistMutation() to filter the finder's own DOM writes out of the debounced MutationObserver rescan) only recognizes:
- the wrap element itself / #oc-wrap / #oc-global-highlight-styles
- Element nodes (nodeType 1) carrying the oc-beacon or oc-viewport-marker class

It does NOT recognize:
1. Text nodes at all (nodeType 3) -- isOculistNode() returns false unconditionally for any text node, even one added as a child of an oculist-owned element.
2. Beacon-descendant elements that don't themselves carry the oc-beacon/oc-viewport-marker class -- e.g. Cyber-Vision's readout div (class oc-cv-readout), a child of the .oc-beacon container.

Concretely: animateCyberVision() sets `readout.textContent = ...`, which creates a text-node child of the readout div. Since neither the readout element nor its new text-node child is recognized as "oculist" by isOculistNode(), isOculistMutation() returns false for this mutation, and startDomObserver()'s callback schedules a genuine rescanAfterMutation() 350ms later on every single Cyber-Vision run.

Impact: if the active match happens to become invisible (e.g. zero-size, display:none) within that 350ms window, the spurious rescan's performListSearch()/findRanges() call filters the match out as invisible and wipes searchRanges to empty ("no match"), even though nothing about the page's real content changed. Confirmed via a temporary diagnostic patch to startDomObserver() while building oculist-3ae's cyber_vision.test.js "stale timer" test -- see that test's forceMatchRediscovery() helper, which works around the gap by forcing a genuine (non-oculist) childList mutation to trigger a real recovery rescan, since a plain style restore is only an attribute change the observer never even sees (it's registered with {childList:true, subtree:true} only).

Fix should generalize isOculistNode() to also recognize:
- text nodes whose parentElement is itself an oculist node (or a similar ancestor-walk), and/or
- elements whose class list starts with oc-cv-/oc- or whose closest oc-beacon ancestor exists

Out of scope for oculist-3ae (which is specifically about the __ocTest hook-reset-before-guard gap in animateChronoTunnel/animateCyberVision), since this is a pre-existing, unrelated MutationObserver filtering gap.

title: seedDefaultBlocklist can erase the welcome wizard's own settings write on first install
description:
Found by the oculist-8s5 reviewer, 2026-08-31, while root-causing a test flake. This is a PRODUCT bug, not a test artifact. Reproduced 5 times in 40 runs.

MECHANISM:
extension/background.js updateSettings() (lines 124-144) does get -> mutate -> set with no compare-and-swap. seedDefaultBlocklist() runs from onInstalled; on a fresh profile its get() snapshots {} BEFORE a concurrent page/popup/wizard write lands, and its set() commits AFTER, erasing that write.

Observed storage state at the moment of failure:
  {"disabledSites":["github.com"],"seededDefaultBlocklist":true}
That is exactly the seed mutation applied to an empty snapshot. The concurrent write, an effect selection, was gone entirely: the key was ABSENT, not stale.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A NARROW RACE:
1. The clobber window coincides with chrome.tabs.create(welcome.html), which background.js opens on the line above. So the setup wizard is launched INSIDE the window in which anything it writes can be silently erased.
2. It does not self-correct. content.js's storage.onChanged handler guards per key with 'if (!(k in nv)) return;' (content.js:7217). The clobbering payload carries no 'effect' key, so an already-open tab keeps its in-memory value forever and never notices. The loss only surfaces on the NEXT page load, in a fresh tab.
3. The wizard tab itself still looks correct while open, because its own state is in memory. The user sees their choice applied, then finds it gone later.
4. Measured window is multi-second under load, not milliseconds. The write happened roughly 1-2s after launch and was still erased.

WHEN IT FIRES: only while seededDefaultBlocklist is falsy, i.e. first install, and an update from a pre-seeding build. That is precisely the moment the wizard runs.

PRIOR ART: oculist-9s9 fixed the background-vs-background case by sequencing both onInstalled writes through one updateSettings(). The comment at background.js:116-123 explicitly documents this remaining background-vs-PAGE window as un-closeable without a CAS primitive chrome.storage does not offer. That is true of CAS specifically, but the bug is still MITIGABLE:
  (a) skip the set() entirely when the mutation changes nothing (the seed already returns false when seededDefaultBlocklist is set; extend that to a genuine no-op check), and/or
  (b) defer seeding until after the welcome tab has been created and had a chance to write, and/or
  (c) re-read and merge immediately before set() rather than writing a snapshot taken earlier.

Verify all line references against the current file before acting; background.js changed under oculist-9s9 and oculist-hzr.

Related: oculist-9s9 (closed), oculist-hzr (closed), oculist-8s5 (the flake this surfaced through).

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Discovered through the oculist-8s5 flake investigation and confirmed as its root cause.

The test-side workaround is committed as 1145a5d on epic/fix-oculist-8s5: test/trail_effect.test.js now forces the effect via the setEffectKey test hook instead of relying on a storage read. That makes the test deterministic but DOES NOT fix this bug, and it removes the only signal the suite currently had for it. Nothing else in the suite would notice this erasure.

That trade is deliberate and recorded, not an oversight: the trail test guards keyboard-only path anchoring, not settings persistence, and the erasure threatens every test that writes settings early. But it does mean this bead is now the only thing tracking the defect.

Reproduction method if it is needed again: run test/trail_effect.test.js repeatedly under CPU load against the tree before 1145a5d, and read chrome.storage.sync from the new tab's isolated world at the moment the assertion fails. 5 hits in 40 runs, every hit showing the same stored object with the effect key absent entirely.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S PREMISE, and the fix that landed.

I filed this bead and its headline scenario was WRONG. Both the implementer and the reviewer independently confirmed from the code: chrome.tabs.create({url: welcome.html}) sits INSIDE seedDefaultBlocklist's done callback, and done is only reached from a set callback (already committed) or the skip path (nothing pending). The wizard tab therefore cannot open until after the seed's write has landed, so the wizard's own write can never race the seed's get-to-set window. 'seedDefaultBlocklist can erase the welcome wizard's own settings write' is unreachable as stated.

The concern was aimed one write site early rather than fabricated: on low-core installs the performanceMode write runs AFTER the wizard tab opens, so THAT write genuinely could race the wizard's write. The fix now recovers it.

THE REAL EXPOSURE, per the reviewer:
- Racers are the <all_urls> document_idle content script (content.js:71 saveSettings does a bare storage.sync.set), popup.js:195/395, and welcome.js:833. None had equivalent protection.
- On INSTALL: low. Chrome does not retro-inject declarative content scripts into already-open tabs and the popup is not open at that instant. Only a page finishing navigation inside the same few-ms window.
- On UPDATE: materially higher, and this is the real case. Live tabs exist, freshly navigated ones inject the new content.js immediately, and the seed still performs a full write on the one update from a pre-seeding build. After that the flag makes mutate return false and no set happens at all, so the hazard is one-shot per profile.
- Severity stays P2 despite the lower likelihood: the loss is silent and PERMANENT, because content.js:7217's 'if (!(k in nv)) return;' means an erased key produces no onChanged entry, so the tab keeps its stale in-memory value and never rewrites it.

FIXED IN 5c2f5b9 with confirm-then-retry optimistic concurrency in updateSettings: re-read and compare against the snapshot mutate ran on, re-run mutate against fresh state on drift, bounded to 3 attempts by observed drift rather than elapsed time. On exhaustion it writes the freshest recomputation, degrading to the old last-writer-wins rather than to data loss. Reviewer verified done fires exactly once across all eight paths, the retry cannot loop, and seed-once semantics survive retries.

title: Four contention flakes make the release gate non-deterministic
description:
Reviewer finding across oculist-rnr.12/.13/.15/.17. Over this epic, npm test rarely produced a clean full run on the first try; the release-gate verification for rnr.17 needed three runs plus an isolation run to establish green.

Four suites fail intermittently under concurrency, all confirmed passing in isolation:
- test/speed_lines.test.js:336 'Lite Mode still draws the centre-line highlight on every frame' (frame-count off by one or two). Tracked separately as oculist-vuk.
- test/trail_effect.test.js:277
- test/worklist_storage.test.js (chrome.storage.session write timeout, 15s)
- test/stale_mount_guard.test.js:176 (waitForFunction 5000ms timeout)

Isolation run of all four together: 26 tests, 26 pass, 0 fail. So these are contention under --test-concurrency=4, not real failures.

Cost: every review in this epic had to re-run and reason about whether a failure was real, which is exactly the judgment a release gate should not require. A gate that cries wolf trains people to wave failures through.

Steps:
1. Identify what the four contend for. Likely candidates: a shared browser instance, real-time frame counting under CPU load, and fixed timeouts sized for an idle machine.
2. Prefer fixing the contention over adding retries. oculist-l6m.32 already converted 106 fixed sleeps to condition polling for this same class of problem; these four look like the residue.
3. Frame-count assertions (speed_lines, trail_effect) should assert a range or a monotonic property, not an exact count, since exact frame counts are wall-clock dependent by nature.
4. If serialization is the answer, mark just these suites rather than dropping concurrency for the whole run.
5. Prove it: run the full suite ten times and require ten clean passes.

Related: oculist-66m (vacuous waitForFunction predicates) touches the same files and should probably be done first or together.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Another data point from the oculist-rnr.19 review (2026-08-30). Across 21 executions on this branch the reviewer saw one failure of the NEW wizard arrow-key test: 4th assertion, '-1' !== '0' — focus had moved and aria-selected had flipped on the sample tab, but its tabindex was still the static -1.

That state is unreachable from the source: the aria-selected and tabindex writes are adjacent lines in the same synchronous forEach. The observed output is byte-identical to a deliberate mutation probe that DELETED the tabindex line, which points at the page having run a stale welcome.js rather than at a logic race.

Corroborating: the same run also flaked speed_lines.test.js, stale_mount_guard.test.js and worklist_storage.test.js, all files untouched by that diff. Isolated runs of the wizard file were 17/17 green, including 12 under 6-way CPU contention.

Reading: environmental (degraded machine and/or a stale extension asset), consistent with this bead's contention-flake thesis. A stale-asset mechanism would be a distinct cause from pure timing contention and may be worth separating out if it recurs.

title: Answering yes to both colour blindness and low vision drops the colour choice
description:
Found by the reviewer during oculist-rnr.13. PRE-EXISTING, not caused by that bead.

In the onboarding wizard, a user who answers yes to a colour-vision question AND yes to low vision loses their colour selection entirely: choosing amber-indigo plus low-vision persists displayPreset 'high-contrast' with colorPalette 'default'. The colour palette they picked is discarded.

This affects exactly the users with the most need, those with more than one vision difference, and it is silent - nothing tells them their colour choice was dropped.

Steps:
1. Reproduce: run the wizard, pick a colour option in step 1 and yes in the low-vision step, then inspect the persisted oc-settings.
2. Decide the correct semantics. Most likely the low-vision preset should compose WITH the chosen palette (sizing and contrast from one, palette from the other) rather than replace it. Confirm the intended behaviour before coding, since this is product semantics.
3. Fix the preset resolution so both answers contribute.
4. Add a test covering every combination of colour answer and low-vision answer.

title: Several tests use waitForFunction predicates that never block
description:
Discovered during oculist-rnr.12 by comparing against a stashed pre-change baseline. Pre-existing, not caused by that bead.

Several *.test.js files check storage writes with a pattern shaped like:
  waitForFunction(() => chrome.storage.sync.get(...).then(d => !!(...)))
The predicate returns a PROMISE, which is always truthy, so waitForFunction resolves immediately on the first poll regardless of whether the underlying condition ever became true. The assertion silently passes even when the value was never written.

Impact: an unknown number of existing storage-write assertions are vacuous. They would not catch a regression in the code they appear to guard. This weakens the suite in exactly the area (settings and list persistence) that the v1.7.0 work depends on.

Steps:
1. Grep test/ for waitForFunction calls whose callback body contains .then( or returns a promise.
2. For each, rewrite to await the storage read and assert on the resolved value, or make the predicate synchronous over already-fetched state, matching whatever pattern the correct tests in the suite already use.
3. Confirm each rewritten assertion FAILS when the behaviour it guards is deliberately broken. A test that cannot fail is not a test.

Do not bulk-rewrite without checking each one - some may be correct already.

title: Marketing site never mentions multi-term lists, v1.7.0's headline feature
description:
repo/docs/index.html is the public marketing site. It was updated for v1.7.0's EFFECTS but not for its headline feature.

Verified 2026-08-30 by grep over repo/docs/:
- 'Speed Lines', 'Chrono Tunnel', 'Cyber-Vision': 2 hits each in index.html. Current.
- 'multi-term', 'search list', 'saved list', 'chip': ZERO hits in index.html.

title: Three copy nits in the v1.7.0 listing description
description:
Second-review findings on oculist-rnr.5. All three are one-word copy edits in /Users/ccho/Documents/Projects/oculist/artifacts/outputs/store-submission-v1.7.0.md. None overclaim privacy or capability, but a wrong count on a public listing is still wrong. Fix before pasting into the dashboard.

title: HUMAN ONLY: check the live listing for the two false claims

Reviewer finding from oculist-rnr.5. Two factual defects found in the v1.7.0 listing copy were INHERITED VERBATIM from artifacts/outputs/store-submission-v1.5.0.md:45-46, not introduced by that bead.
