title: content.js onChanged listener never refreshes the settings merge base
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-xvh. That bead gave the page-side writers a three-way merge (OculistSettingsMigration.writeOcSettings) against a per-context base snapshot recorded by rememberOcSettings().

content.js's chrome.storage.onChanged listener (around extension/content.js:7222) updates the in-memory 'settings' object from a foreign write but never calls rememberOcSettings(), so 'base' stays at the boot snapshot until this tab's own next successful write.

Losing sequence, needs two foreign writes to the same key straddling a local save:
1. base.X = v1 at boot.
2. Foreign write sets X = v2. The listener adopts v2 into in-memory settings; base still says v1.
3. Foreign write sets X = v3. Suppose the listener has not yet applied it, or the tab saves first.
4. This tab calls saveSettings(). The merge sees local.X (v2) != base.X (v1), so it treats v2 as a local edit and it wins -> v3 is silently reverted to v2.

Narrow, but exactly the lost-update class oculist-xvh set out to close, so it should not be left standing.

FIX: call OculistSettingsMigration.rememberOcSettings() from the onChanged listener whenever it adopts a foreign change, so base tracks what the tab believes storage holds. Take care that base and the in-memory settings object are updated from the SAME payload and in the same pass - if base advances but the local object does not, a genuine local edit is lost instead, which is the worse direction.

Note content.js only merges SETTINGS_KEYS into its in-memory settings, while base should reflect the whole stored object. Decide deliberately whether rememberOcSettings() is handed the full new stored value or only the allowlisted subset, and write down which and why - the merge's deletion rule (a key in base but absent from local is treated as a deliberate deletion) makes this choice load-bearing. See the comment at extension/settings-migration.js:161-171.

title: PRIVACY.md says the reseed runs on every update, but it also runs on install
description:
Confirmed independently by two reviewers during oculist-3yi. A genuine scope understatement in a user-facing privacy disclosure, which is the unsafe direction.

PRIVACY.md (around lines 70-71) says the default disabled-sites reseed 'runs once on every update'. The code runs it on INSTALL too: seedDefaultBlocklist() is called at extension/background.js:198, directly in the onInstalled listener body and OUTSIDE the 'if (details.reason === 'install')' check at :199, so it is unconditional for every reason the event fires.

Why it matters rather than being a nit: a disclosure that understates when a step runs is narrower than the code, and narrower is the unsafe direction for a privacy policy. Everywhere else in these documents the wording is deliberately kept broader than the code.

Not purely theoretical on install: on a REINSTALL with Chrome Sync restoring a previous settings object, details.reason === 'install' and the seed runs against a non-empty object that may still carry a legacy key. It is only harmless on a genuinely fresh profile, where the object is empty and there is nothing to carry forward.

FIX: change 'runs once on every update' to cover install as well, e.g. 'runs once on every install and every update'. description:
Sibling survey done during oculist-47e, confirmed independently by that bead's reviewer. The pattern holds in 3 of 3 effects that hang test state off __ocTest, so it is systemic to the idiom rather than isolated.

oculist-47e fixed animateSpeedLines: its early-return guard (rect.width===0 || rect.height===0) sat ahead of every __ocTest assignment, so a skipped run left all ten hooks holding the PREVIOUS run's values. A test polling speedLinesDone === true would resolve instantly off stale state and grade everything else against that stale run.

SAME DEFECT, NOT YET FIXED:
1. animateChronoTunnel (extension/content.js ~2638): the guard precedes lastChronoHueRun (~2721), lastChronoAnchor (~2726), chronoFrameCount (~2727) and chronoDone (~2728).
   This one is arguably WORSE than speed lines was: lastChronoHueRun.hueSamples.push(...) runs inside the frame loop, so a stale object keeps ACCUMULATING samples across runs rather than merely being read stale.
2. animateCyberVision (extension/content.js ~2827): the guard precedes cyberVisionBracketsSettled (~3000).

NOT AFFECTED, verified: animateTrail and animateDispersion contain no __ocTest references, and neither do the other nine animate* functions. There are 59 __ocTest lines in the file, none inside those functions and none after ~3002.

FIX DIRECTION: mirror oculist-47e — reset the effect's whole hook set at the very top of the function, before the guard, using values that mean 'this run produced nothing'. Do not fix one hook in isolation; the done-flag shares the same gap and is what makes a stale run look complete.

Note what oculist-47e's review established: a zero-metric match IS reachable through the normal path, because a span with font-size:0 yields a zero Range rect and is still indexed (buildPageIndex only skips display:none / visibility:hidden). So these can be tested through a real fixture match without exposing the effect functions on __ocTest.

title: Page-side settings writers have no lost-update protection
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-b65. That bead hardened only background.js; this is the larger half of the same race surface.

oculist-b65 gave extension/background.js's updateSettings() confirm-then-retry optimistic concurrency so a concurrent write landing in its get-to-set gap is detected and recovered. The page-side writers got no equivalent and each still does a bare read-modify-write or a bare set:
- extension/content.js:71 saveSettings() does a bare chrome.storage.sync.set
- extension/popup.js:195 and :395
- extension/welcome.js:833 saveProfileAndFinish()

Any two of these racing each other, or racing background.js, can still silently lose a write. Same permanence problem as b65: content.js:7217's onChanged handler guards per key with 'if (!(k in nv)) return;', so a key erased by a clobbering write produces no change entry and an open tab keeps its stale in-memory value indefinitely.

Realistic shape: the popup and an open page both writing settings, or the welcome wizard finishing while a content script persists something.

Likely fix: lift b65's confirm-then-retry into a shared helper both surfaces use. Note background.js is a service worker loading settings-migration.js via importScripts, while the page surfaces load it as a script tag, so the helper needs to work in both contexts the way settings-migration.js already does.

title: Revisit PRIVACY.md's reseed wording now that background.js normalizes on every write
description:
Filed during oculist-rnr.23 (2026-08-31). Retitled and written up because the original title, 'overstates current risk', with an EMPTY description, reads cold as a mandate to narrow a privacy disclosure to match code. It is not. Read the whole of this before touching PRIVACY.md.

WHAT CHANGED IN THE CODE. Two beads landed after PRIVACY.md's reseed paragraph was written:
- oculist-9s9 routed both onInstalled write sites through one updateSettings() helper and sequenced the performanceMode write inside seedDefaultBlocklist()'s done callback.
- oculist-hzr added importScripts('settings-migration.js') to background.js, so normalizeOcSettings() now runs at that single choke point ahead of every mutate() and set().
Net effect, verified by two agents: on the NORMAL path neither write can persist an unmigrated legacy visionProfile, including the case that originally motivated the concern (seededDefaultBlocklist already true from a cross-profile sync, seed early-returns, performanceMode write still normalizes).

WHY THIS IS NOT A DEFECT. PRIVACY.md's disclosure ('can write the old key back once, the next read removes it') is still TRUE. background.js declares OculistSettingsMigration = null and only assigns it inside a try/catch, so if importScripts ever fails (packaging mistake, or a browser without it) normalization is skipped for both write sites and the originally-disclosed behaviour is exactly what happens. The disclosure now describes that guarded fallback rather than the common case.

BEING BROADER THAN THE CODE IS THE SAFE DIRECTION FOR A PRIVACY DISCLOSURE. Do NOT narrow this text merely because the common path improved. If it is ever revisited:
1. Re-verify the importScripts guard still exists and still fails closed. If that guard is ever removed and normalization becomes unconditional, only THEN does the fallback disappear.
2. PRIVACY.md and docs/privacy.html are a KEEP IN SYNC pair. Any change lands in both or they diverge.
3. test/privacy_invariants.test.js asserts across both files. Read it first.
4. artifacts/outputs/store-submission-v1.7.0.md (outer repo) carries the reasoning above in its Health/Data-usage commentary and would need to stay consistent.

The genuinely useful outcome here may simply be a sentence in PRIVACY.md noting the re-persist is now limited to a fallback path, leaving the conservative claim intact. Verify all line references against current files before editing.

title: animateSpeedLines early-return leaves all __ocTest hooks (not just lastSpeedLinesContainerRect) holding the previous run's stale values
description:
animateSpeedLines(rect) returns early at the top (rect.width===0 || rect.height===0) before ANY of its __ocTest hooks are touched: lastSpeedLinesStreakCount, speedLinesFrameCount, lastSpeedLinesLaneAlphaMax, lastSpeedLinesElseAlphaMax, speedLinesHighlightDrawCount, speedLinesDone, lastSpeedLinesAnchor, lastSpeedLinesHighlightY, and lastSpeedLinesContainerRect are all reset/set together, well after the guard. On a skipped run every one of these retains the PREVIOUS run's value -- not just the container rect. A test that polls e.g. speedLinesDone === true would resolve immediately off stale prior-run state, then grade every other hook (including the container rect) against that same stale run, without ever surfacing that the current run never actually fired.

Noted while working oculist-gor (container rect is viewport-relative, scroll-staleness). Fixing lastSpeedLinesContainerRect's staleness alone would not close this exposure since speedLinesDone shares the identical gap, so it was deliberately left alone there for consistency with the rest of the hooks.

Fix direction: reset the whole set of speed-lines __ocTest hooks together at the very top of animateSpeedLines (before the early-return check), or introduce a shared "run started" marker/counter the test suite can check to detect a skipped run, rather than fixing one hook in isolation. No test currently exercises the rect.width===0 path, so this is a latent exposure, not a live failure.

title: background.js can still resurrect a legacy settings key the popup deleted
description:
Split out of oculist-9s9, which closed on a narrower fix (serializing background.js's own two writes). This half was verified still-open by that bead's reviewer.

REPRODUCED against the CURRENT code, not theoretical:
  T0 initial:      {disabledSites: [], visionProfile: 'legacy-deuteranopia'}
  T1 popup wrote:  {disabledSites: [], colorProfile: 'deuteranopia'}
  FINAL:           {disabledSites: ['github.com'], visionProfile: 'legacy-deuteranopia', seededDefaultBlocklist: true}
  visionProfile resurrected: true. popup's colorProfile: lost.

MECHANISM: seedDefaultBlocklist()'s get() is the first thing in the onInstalled listener and is no fresher than before oculist-9s9. If the popup normalizes settings and writes between that get() and its set(), background writes back the stale object, resurrecting the legacy key the popup just deleted and dropping the popup's own write. oculist-9s9 only shortened the performanceMode write's window, not the seed's.

WHY BACKGROUND IS THE ONLY PATH THAT CAN DO THIS: background.js does not load settings-migration.js, so its write-back never passes through normalizeOcSettings(). Every other surface normalizes.

THE REAL FIX is loading settings-migration.js into the service worker, which was deliberately scoped OUT of oculist-9s9 because it needs a manifest change. background.js is a classic (non-module) service worker per manifest.json, so importScripts('settings-migration.js') is the likely mechanism. Confirm that against the manifest before assuming it.

NOTE the user-visible outcome is already disclosed in the privacy policy ('can write the old key back once, the next read removes it'), so nothing is misstated to users. This is about the code.

title: speed_lines Lite Mode test passes only because of test ordering
description:
Found by the oculist-z4s reviewer while verifying that bead's fix. PRE-EXISTING and verified against unmodified HEAD, so NOT caused by the z4s change.

test/speed_lines.test.js 'Lite Mode still draws the centre-line highlight on every frame' passes in the full suite but FAILS when run alone:
  node --test --test-name-pattern='Lite Mode still draws' test/speed_lines.test.js
It fails on .oc-beacon already being torn down. The reviewer confirmed it fails identically on the unmodified HEAD version, so this is latent order-dependence, not a regression.

Mechanism: the test's speedLinesDone wait is satisfied by a STALE flag left by a prior effect's orphaned rAF loop. replay() removes the container from the DOM without cancelling that loop, so the flag from the earlier run is still set when this test checks it. That is also why the atomic read lands mid-flight rather than after completion.

Consequences:
1. The test does not actually wait for its own effect to finish, so 'draws on every frame' is only ever checked over an arbitrary partial prefix of the run.
2. A release-gate suite contains a test that depends on execution order, which will surface as a mystery failure the first time someone runs it in isolation or the file order changes.

Fix direction: cancel the rAF loop in replay() (or scope the done flag per run) so the wait gates on THIS run's completion, then re-check what the assertion is actually covering.

Related: oculist-z4s (closed), oculist-8s5, oculist-3z6.

title: loadWorkList/saveWorkList silently drop writes and reads denied by storage.session access level
description:
Product bug found while root-causing the oculist-z4s test flake. NOT a test-harness artifact. Assessed by the z4s reviewer as P3 hardening, not a release blocker.

MECHANISM (verified in code by two agents):
background.js:8-18 calls chrome.storage.session.setAccessLevel('TRUSTED_AND_UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS') as fire-and-forget service-worker top-level code with only a .catch logger. There is no ordering relationship between that grant and content-script boot.

content.js:163-183 saveWorkList() guards only on chrome.storage.session being UNDEFINED. In the racing case the API is defined-but-denied, so the guard does not fire, and the rejection is swallowed twice: 'void chrome.runtime.lastError;' in the callback and 'setResult.catch(function () {});'. No retry, no log, no signal. A write that loses the race is dropped permanently.

Measured: 2 of 15 cold launches had the content-script write land before the access grant, once by only 9ms, each producing an immediate (~2ms) chrome.runtime.lastError 'Access to storage is not allowed from this context.'

REACHABILITY (reviewer's assessment):
- Write side is close to unreachable in production. All four persistWorkList() callers (content.js:4286, 4310, 4410, 5450) require an already-open overlay, which only opens after background.js round-trips the command, plus seconds of human typing before any write.
- READ side is the reachable one. buildUI()'s loadWorkList() (content.js:5909) fires one message hop after SW start and, on lastError, silently returns defaultWorkList(). The user sees their carried-over list vanish, and the next chip mutation then persists over the stored list.
- Mitigating: the access level is a property of the session storage area and normally survives SW restarts, so the vulnerable window is before the first successful grant, when session storage is empty anyway and the default is the correct answer. NOT confirmed from code whether Chrome ever resets it on SW restart. That uncertainty is the residual risk and is the thing to establish first.

SUGGESTED FIX: on an access-denied chrome.runtime.lastError, retry once (or gate first storage use on a background ready-ping) in BOTH loadWorkList and saveWorkList, and log instead of unconditionally swallowing. The unconditional swallow currently makes any real storage failure undiagnosable, which also cuts against this repo's debug-logging guideline.

title: Wizard reset has no working regression guard
description:

title: Mapping tables duplicated in popup.js and welcome.js instead of importing the module's export
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-rnr.12 (non-blocking, work already shipped correctly).

extension/settings-migration.js is the canonical home for the legacy-to-functional mapping, and it EXPORTS the tables. But two consumers keep their own verbatim copies rather than referencing the export:
- extension/popup.js:104-111 LEGACY_TO_FUNCTIONAL_PRESET, a verbatim duplicate of LEGACY_DISPLAY_PRESET_MAP.
- extension/welcome.js:35-41 WIZARD_PROFILE_TO_DISPLAY_PRESET, the same table minus 'custom'.

They are consistent today, so nothing is broken. The risk is drift: a future edit to the canonical table silently diverges from two copies, and the module docstring's claim that it is 'the one place it lives' is true of the normaliser but not of the tables.

Steps:
1. Have popup.js and welcome.js reference the exported tables from window.OculistSettingsMigration instead of declaring their own.
2. Preserve welcome.js's 'custom' exclusion explicitly at the point of use rather than by maintaining a trimmed copy of the table.
3. If a copy must remain for load-order reasons, prove it with a test that asserts the copies equal the canonical table, so drift fails the suite.
4. Correct the module docstring to match whatever ends up true.

ALSO, from the same review: no test seeds visionProfile AND displayPreset together, so the hasOwnProperty precedence branch in settings-migration.js:71-78 (new field wins, legacy deleted) is verified by inspection only. Add that test - it guards the exact behaviour that prevents user data loss.
