title: Fix clipped box-shadow glow on Impact Burst effect
description: In repo/extension/content.js, animateImpactBurst()'s burst-shape element has both clip-path (for the star polygon) and box-shadow (for glow) — clip-path clips box-shadow, so the glow never renders. Move the glow to a separate unclipped element behind the star, or drop the box-shadow. Cosmetic only, found during review of oculist-y9h.1.
close_reason: Obsolete — the Impact Burst effect (oculist-y9h.1) was reverted in 2554612, so animateImpactBurst() and its clipped box-shadow no longer exist in extension/content.js. Re-file if the effect is ever reintroduced.

title: animateSpeedLines and animateChronoTunnel will use different container-removal idioms
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-3ae. Only bites once oculist-3ae lands.

oculist-3ae (branch wip/oculist-3ae) moves animateChronoTunnel's container.remove() out of its standalone setTimeout(DUR) and into frame()'s own completion branch, so removal is strictly after the last frame by construction. animateSpeedLines keeps the old setTimeout(DUR) idiom.

That leaves the two sibling canvas effects removing their containers in different ways for no reason a reader can see. Worse, the comment at extension/content.js around :2400 justifies lastSpeedLinesContainerRect's capture-early design specifically in terms of the removal timer racing the completion tick - which will read as contradicting chrono's new note saying that race is why the timer was removed.

animateSpeedLines cannot produce chrono's crash: its frame loop only ASSIGNS to hooks (lastSpeedLinesHighlightY, the counters), never reads a property off an object a later run can null. Its exposure is silent count inflation - speedLinesFrameCount and the alpha-max hooks can each be advanced by one stale frame - not a throw. So this is consistency and comment accuracy, not a live defect.

DO: after oculist-3ae lands, either move animateSpeedLines to the same completion-branch removal, or write down at both sites why they deliberately differ. Then reconcile the :2400 comment with whichever is true. Note oculist-qii (fadeActiveBeacons orphaning rAF loops) hits animateSpeedLines too, so check whether fixing that changes the answer here.

Verify all line references against current files before acting.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Not actionable yet - confirmed against the tree, not assumed. Both animateSpeedLines and animateChronoTunnel still use the same setTimeout(DUR) self-removal idiom on main, so the divergence this bead describes does not exist yet. It only appears if oculist-3ae lands its completion-branch removal for chrono.

Doing this bead now would mean moving BOTH effects to completion-branch removal, which is oculist-3ae's fix applied under a bead that does not authorize it. Left alone deliberately.

Added dependencies on oculist-3ae and on oculist-qii - qii's destroyBeacon teardown also touches animateSpeedLines, and the bead's own text says to check whether that changes the answer here.

title: settings_race test (a) monkeypatches Array.prototype.push across an await
description:
Reviewer test-hygiene nit from oculist-6tp. Not a defect today; a trap for a future change.

test/settings_race.test.js's new case (a) - 'a mutate that throws synchronously still calls done exactly once and issues no set' - forces the throw by monkeypatching Array.prototype.push process-wide, narrowed to the single one-argument 'github.com' call, and restores it in a finally.

Why it is currently safe: node's test runner runs top-level tests within one file sequentially, the patch is narrowed to one specific argument value, it self-restores, and the finally is a net. So the blast radius is small.

Why it is still worth removing: it depends on DEFAULT_DISABLED_SITES containing 'github.com' and on push being reached with exactly one argument. Change the seed list in extension/background.js and the test either stops exercising the throw path (silently passing for the wrong reason) or patches a different call than intended. A process-wide prototype patch held across an await is also the kind of thing that breaks once anything in the file runs concurrently.

FIX: make the mutate throw directly instead. The test calls updateSettings with its own mutate, so a mutate that throws on its own needs no prototype patching at all. If the intent was specifically to make seedDefaultBlocklist's OWN mutate throw (rather than an arbitrary caller's), inject the failure through the fake chrome.storage.sync so the stored 'oc-settings' is a non-object - that is the reachable production trigger the bead named, and it exercises the same path without touching a global prototype.

Verify the rewritten test still fails against the pre-fix background.js (git show <commit-before-e730819>:extension/background.js) - it must, or it has stopped testing anything.

title: reduced-motion beacons are never faded on scroll
description:
Reviewer finding during oculist-5rv. Pre-existing; 5rv did not introduce it, but 5rv's new test (c) now pins the current behaviour, so fixing this means updating that test too.

extension/content.js's animate() routes motion === 'reduced' to animateReducedMotion(rect) and RETURNS before reaching the activeBeacons++ site. animateReducedMotion() does draw a .oc-beacon element. So on the reduced-motion path the flag reads 0 while a beacon is on the page.

Consequence: fadeActiveBeacons() opens with 'if (activeBeacons === 0) return;' and is the scroll path's entry point (handleScroll, extension/content.js around :4949). With the flag at 0 it early-returns, so a reduced-motion beacon is never faded out on scroll the way a full-motion one is. It is still removed by cancelBeacons() on the next search or navigation, so this is a missing fade, not a permanent artifact.

This is the opposite direction from the oculist-5rv leak: that one over-counted (a wasted querySelectorAll), this one under-counts (a real behaviour gap), and under-counting is the direction that actually suppresses work.

DECIDE FIRST, then fix: is the reduced-motion beacon MEANT to survive a scroll? Users on this path have asked for less motion, and a fade is itself motion, so leaving it pinned until the next search may well be deliberate. Check git history and any reduced-motion notes in content.js before changing behaviour.

- If it is deliberate: leave the code alone and replace the incidental behaviour with an explicit comment at the animateReducedMotion branch in animate() saying the flag is deliberately not raised, and why. Update test (c) in test/active_beacons_counter.test.js to assert that intent rather than merely observing it.
- If it is not deliberate: raise the flag on the reduced-motion path too, guarded by the same zero-rect condition the full-motion site now uses, and update test (c).

Either way the outcome is that the asymmetry is stated on purpose instead of being an accident that a test happens to enshrine.

Verify all line references against current files before acting.

title: activeBeacons leaks on a guard-skipped effect run
description:
Reviewer finding during oculist-47e. PRE-EXISTING at HEAD; that bead did not introduce it, but its new zero-size-rect test makes the path reachable by test for the first time.

extension/content.js's animate() does activeBeacons++ BEFORE calling effectObj.run(rect). When the effect's own early-return guard fires (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0), run() returns immediately having created no beacon, so the counter is incremented with no matching decrement. Every guard-skipped run leaks one.

Reachable in production, not just in tests: a zero-metric match is a static fixture property, not a timing race. A span with font-size:0 yields a zero Range rect and is still indexed, because buildPageIndex only skips display:none and visibility:hidden. So a page containing such text produces real matches that reach the guard on every navigation to them.

What to check when picking this up:
- What activeBeacons actually gates. If it feeds a cap or a cleanup decision, a slow leak could eventually suppress beacons entirely for the life of the page.
- Whether the fix belongs in animate() (increment only after run() has committed to drawing) or in each effect's guard (decrement before the early return). Prefer the single site in animate() over touching every effect.
- oculist-3ae covers the sibling effects' stale-hook defect and touches the same guards; consider doing them together.

Verify line references against the current file before acting.

title: background.js swallows done and lastError on storage failure paths
description:
Two reviewer findings from oculist-b65. Both pre-existing and structurally unchanged by that fix.

1. A synchronous throw inside the mutate callback passed to updateSettings() propagates out of the storage callback and 'done' NEVER FIRES. Because seedDefaultBlocklist's done is what calls chrome.tabs.create(welcome.html), that means no welcome tab on install. There is no try/catch around the mutate(settings) call. Reachable if oc-settings is ever stored as a non-object, or if a future mutate throws.
   Precedent for the fix and the test shape: oculist-ex1 and oculist-idd solved the analogous exactly-once callback problem in content.js's loadWorkList, and test/worklist_storage.test.js already has a case '(e) a synchronous get() callback whose caller callback throws still calls back exactly once'.

2. chrome.runtime.lastError is checked on NEITHER the get nor the set inside updateSettings(). A failed get yields {} and the seed would then write a near-empty settings object over whatever is stored. A failed set opens the welcome tab as if the write had succeeded, verified by probe.

Both are in extension/background.js's updateSettings(). Verify line references against the current file; it changed under oculist-9s9, hzr and b65.

title: lastSpeedLinesContainerRect is viewport-relative and goes stale on scroll
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-viv. Not a defect today; a documented limitation of the approach that bead introduced.

oculist-viv fixed a teardown race by capturing window.__ocTest.lastSpeedLinesContainerRect via getBoundingClientRect() right after the beacon container is appended, and having the speed_lines Lite Mode test compare it against a LIVE #target rect.

The container itself is position:absolute with fixed left/top/width/height/transform set before append, so its DOCUMENT-coordinate position never moves. But getBoundingClientRect() is VIEWPORT-relative. Any scroll between the capture and the test's read makes the captured rect stale by the scroll delta and would produce a false dy in the '|highlightY - independent.y| <= 2' assertion.

The previous version read both rects live at the same instant and was scroll-robust; this one is not. It holds today only because the test page is static and never scrolls. It would break if this pattern were reused on a scrolling page, or if a scroll-settle re-anchor step were added to the effect.

Options: capture scrollX/scrollY alongside the rect and correct for the delta at read time, or convert both sides to document coordinates.

Also noted, pre-existing and not introduced by viv: if animateSpeedLines returns early (rect.width === 0), lastSpeedLinesContainerRect retains the PREVIOUS run's value, so the test would grade against a stale rect rather than failing on a null independent. The other __ocTest hooks share this exposure.

title: Tighten try/catch scope in attemptLoadWorkList and retryAfterSessionAccessReady
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-ex1. Unreachable in real Chrome; live under the test mocks.

attemptLoadWorkList's outer try/catch wraps the chrome.storage.session.get CALL. If get ever invoked its callback synchronously and the caller's callback threw, the throw would land in that outer catch and fire callback(defaultWorkList()) a SECOND time. loadWorkList explicitly guards this hazard on its !storageAvailable path and says so in a comment; attemptLoadWorkList does not.

Real storage.session.get is always async, so production is safe. But the oculist-ex1 test mocks DO invoke cb() synchronously, so the hazard is live under mocks and could mask or manufacture a double-invocation in a future test.

Same shape in retryAfterSessionAccessReady: next() is called INSIDE the try, so a synchronous sendMessage mock plus a throwing next() would run next() twice.

Fix: tighten each try to wrap only the chrome API call itself, not the callback dispatch. That closes both.

Separately, pre-existing and unrelated: content.js:7129's chrome.runtime.onMessage listener dereferences msg.action with no null guard. Verify line numbers before editing.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Closed. Reviewer note worth keeping: retryAfterSessionAccessReady's 'if (reachedCallback) throw err;' has ZERO test coverage, because every sendMessage mock in the suite delegates to the real async API. It is defensive symmetry with the load path and correct by construction, but untested. Not filed as its own bead: in production the try has always exited before the handler runs, so that line is dead code there, and a test would have to fabricate a synchronous sendMessage mock.

Also noted, pre-existing and out of scope: attemptSaveWorkList's empty catch would likewise swallow an error rethrown from a nested retry. Nothing observable depends on it.

title: runMockupAnimation reads module-level selectedProfile instead of its resolved settings
description:
Reviewer note from oculist-336. Pre-existing, not introduced by that bead. Not currently reachable as a defect.

oculist-336 routed the wizard's preset composition through a single resolveVisionSettings(), consumed by buildPreviewSummary(), runMockupAnimation() and saveProfileAndFinish().

One stale read survives: runMockupAnimation() still reads the module-level selectedProfile at extension/welcome.js:495, inside the motion === 'reduced' branch, rather than the resolved object it took at the top of the function.

Why it is not a live bug: only the eye-strain preset sets motionSensitivity 'reduced', and the low-vision palette overlay cannot reach that branch, so the two values agree today.

Why it is worth closing: it is the one remaining place where the mockup animation can diverge from the resolver if the preset tables ever change which profiles use reduced motion. Verify the line reference against the current file before editing.

title: readStoredSettings is duplicated verbatim across 12 test files
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-66m. Not a defect.

The oculist-66m fix introduced a local readStoredSettings(target) helper into each of the 11 files it touched; counting the pre-existing copy in test/vision_profile_survives_ungoverned_toggle.test.js that is 12 verbatim copies. It belongs in test/helpers/ alongside waitForCondition (test/helpers/wait.js), which is already shared.

Also worth considering: the oculist-66m reviewer wrote a paren-balancing scanner that walks every waitForFunction( call site in test/ and flags any predicate containing async, .then( or await. That is a cheap structural guard against this defect shape reappearing. Landing it as a test would make the class of bug self-policing rather than relying on someone grepping for it again.

title: Wizard tablist: four untested paths left by rnr.19
description:
Reviewer follow-ups from oculist-rnr.19. The implementation is correct by reading; these are coverage gaps, each roughly a one-liner to close.

1. resetWizardState()'s roving-tabindex restore is COMPLETELY unguarded. Reviewer probe: corrupt the tabindex assignment on the reset path only, leave everything else intact, and the suite stays GREEN (7 pass / 0 fail). Best home is the rnr.18 reset test in test/wizard_no_clinical_persistence.test.js, which already asserts the reopened wizard is on the named tab: add that the named tab is also the tabindex=0 stop.
2. Home/End are implemented in the keydown handler but untested.
3. preventDefault scoping is untested. The handler correctly returns before preventDefault for unhandled keys, so Tab/Enter/Space pass through natively, but nothing asserts it.
4. The keyboard-reachability guarantee is asserted only in halves, never end to end. Roving tabindex removed the sample tab's own Tab stop; the replacement path is ArrowRight to reach it. One test proves arrows reveal the sample panel, another proves a CLICK-opened panel's options are Tab-reachable and well-named, but no test walks arrow-then-Tab through to the options behind the unselected tab.

Also: the comment at test/wizard_no_clinical_persistence.test.js:223 ('Tabs themselves must be keyboard reachable too') is now stale under roving tabindex. The assertion beneath it only checks accessible name and remains valid; just the comment misleads.

title: dim_contrast.test.js hand-copies the preset mapping table instead of importing it
description:
Follow-up raised by both the implementer and reviewer on oculist-rnr.22.

test/dim_contrast.test.js:33-34 declares its own literal LEGACY_TO_FUNCTIONAL_PRESET with a comment saying it mirrors popup.js. It is used at :376. Because it is a copy, drift between it and the canonical extension/settings-migration.js export would go undetected: the test would keep passing against a stale table.

test/display_preset_migration.test.js:27,40 has similar literal copies, left in place by rnr.22.

Fix: have these tests read the canonical table via require('../extension/settings-migration.js') the way the rnr.22 tests now do, or assert the copy equals the export.

Also noted (separate, smaller): the Object.freeze added in rnr.22 is shallow. Correct today since both tables hold only string values, but it stops protecting if either ever gains a nested object value.

title: Doc assumes the reseed is the only unmigrated write on onInstalled
description:
Reviewer follow-up from oculist-rnr.20, not a defect in that bead's terms.

store-submission-v1.7.0.md says the performanceMode write's carried-forward value is 'the same transient artifact already covered by the disclosed reseed exception above, not a second, separate one.'

Strictly it is a second CODE PATH: if seededDefaultBlocklist is already true (synced in from another profile), seedDefaultBlocklist() early-returns at background.js:70 while the performanceMode write still re-persists the whole settings object.

The user-visible artifact and its self-correction are identical, so the claim holds as written about the artifact. The risk is forward-looking: a future edit to PRIVACY.md's disclosure must not assume the reseed step is the only unmigrated write on that event.

Verify line references against the code before acting.

title: Freeze the exported mapping table and guard the reverse-table derivation
description:
Two reviewer follow-ups from oculist-rnr.16. Neither is a current defect; both are structural hardening of the migration path.

1. popup.js's LEGACY_TO_FUNCTIONAL_PRESET is now a live ALIAS of the module's exported table, not a copy. Both call sites are read-only today, so nothing is wrong, but a future write through that alias would silently corrupt the canonical table for content.js as well, since they share the object. Object.freeze on the export would make the read-only contract structural rather than conventional.

2. popup.js derives FUNCTIONAL_TO_LEGACY_PRESET by inverting the canonical table at load time. That inversion is correct ONLY while every forward value stays distinct. All six are distinct today (verified: no key collision, custom->custom is a self-map and survives). A future duplicate forward value would silently drop a reverse entry, with no test guarding it. Add an assertion that the inverted table has the same entry count as the forward one, so a collision fails the suite rather than degrading the popup's dropdown silently.

title: Store copy implies match markers always appear
description:
Reviewer note from oculist-rnr.8. Both store docs say Oculist 'only ever adds its own overlay, a style element, and match markers'. The marker dots at content.js:4715-4731 are gated on a colorblind palette (isColorBlind check ~4677, early-returns otherwise), so they do NOT always appear.

Over-inclusive rather than false: the sentence describes the maximum set of things added, which is the right direction for a privacy claim. PRIVACY.md already uses narrower framing.

The identical sentence is in BOTH store-submission-v1.5.0.md and store-submission-v1.7.0.md, byte-identical by design so the two agree. Any fix must change both together or they diverge. Low priority; do not fix one alone.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Deferred by the unattended /goal run on 2026-08-30 — needs an operator decision, not an agent guess.

Verified state: the sentence is byte-identical at store-submission-v1.5.0.md:54 and store-submission-v1.7.0.md:61 ('Oculist only ever adds its own overlay, a style element, and match markers'). It sits inside the user-facing '★ WORKS ON REAL PAGES' listing description, i.e. transcribed dashboard copy, not internal commentary.

Why it was not actioned unattended:
1. The bead's own analysis says the claim is over-inclusive rather than false — 'only ever adds X, Y, Z' is a maximum-set bound, which is the correct direction for a privacy claim. So doing nothing is a defensible outcome.
2. Any edit changes copy the human pastes into the Developer Dashboard, and interacts with oculist-rnr.8 (checking the live listing). That is re-transcription work an agent should not create on its own.

Options for the human:
(a) Leave as-is. The maximum-set framing is accurate and conservative; close as wontfix.
(b) Soften to name the conditionality, e.g. '...its own overlay, a style element, and (on colour-vision palettes) match markers'. Must be applied to BOTH docs in the same commit or they diverge.

Evidence: marker dots are gated on a colourblind palette check in content.js and early-return otherwise — re-verify the line numbers against the current file before editing, the bead's ~4677/4715-4731 refs are from 2026-08-30 and may have shifted.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
CLOSED as wontfix. Human decision 2026-08-31: leave the sentence as it stands.

The sentence, byte-identical at store-submission-v1.5.0.md:54 and store-submission-v1.7.0.md:61:
  'Oculist only ever adds its own overlay, a style element, and match markers'

Reasoning, which this bead itself already reached: 'only ever adds X, Y, Z' is a MAXIMUM-SET bound. It states the ceiling on what the extension puts on a page; it does not promise all three always appear. Two further reasons not to touch it:

The suggested wording was '...its own overlay, a style element, and (on colour-vision palettes) match markers'.

Evidence, unchanged: the marker dots are gated on a colourblind palette check in content.js and early-return otherwise. Re-verify the line numbers against the current file before acting; the refs recorded on 2026-08-30 have since shifted.

title: seedDefaultBlocklist read-modify-write is not atomic
description: Reviewer note from oculist-rnr.14, code robustness, not a doc gap. background.js:67-78 seedDefaultBlocklist() reads oc-settings, mutates, and writes the whole object back. That read/modify/write is not atomic, so a popup opened concurrently with an extension update can interleave with it and lose one side's write. The user-visible outcome is already disclosed in the privacy policy ('can write the old key back once, the next read removes it'), so nothing is misstated; this is about the code being racy. Also note background.js does not load settings-migration.js, so its write-back is the one path that can re-persist a legacy key.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Closed on a NARROWER outcome than the title implies. Recording exactly what was and was not fixed, verified by the reviewer against the code.

FIXED: background.js clobbering its OWN earlier write. onInstalled previously issued both get() calls synchronously before either set() landed, so the performanceMode set() committed a snapshot predating the seed set() and erased it. Both sites now route through one updateSettings(), and the performanceMode write runs inside the seed's done callback, so its read follows the seed's commit.

NOT FIXED, still open: the bead's headline complaint. A popup interleaving with an extension update can still lose a write. The window between each individual get() and its own set() is unchanged in width and count. chrome.storage.sync has no transaction or compare-and-swap primitive, so that window cannot be closed without an API Chrome does not offer. This is stated in a comment at the helper rather than papered over.

NOT FIXED, still open: the legacy-key resurrection. The seed's get() is at the identical point in time as before, so nothing changed for that write. The reviewer reproduced the bead's exact scenario against the NEW code:
  T0 initial: {disabledSites:[], visionProfile:'legacy-deuteranopia'}
  T1 popup wrote: {disabledSites:[], colorProfile:'deuteranopia'}
  FINAL: {disabledSites:['github.com'], visionProfile:'legacy-deuteranopia', seededDefaultBlocklist:true}
  visionProfile resurrected: true. popup colorProfile lost: true.
Only the performanceMode write's resurrection window shrank. Filed as a follow-up.

LATENT COUPLING introduced, not a live bug: the welcome tab's chrome.tabs.create is now deferred inside the seed's done callback rather than firing synchronously, so it would not fire if mutate threw. Neither mutate has a throw path today (disabledSites is normalized to an array first) and chrome.storage callbacks always fire.

TEST CAVEAT: test/settings_race.test.js's injected 'concurrent write' lands before the second get() is issued, so it survives under the old implementation too. comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Investigated at length during the unattended /goal run 2026-08-30/31 on branch epic/oculist-flakes-and-bugs. NO FIX MADE, deliberately. Working tree left clean. Findings below so this is not re-derived from scratch.

=== THE z4s ACCESS-RACE HYPOTHESIS IS RULED OUT FOR THESE FLAKES ===
oculist-z4s root-caused worklist_storage's flake to a chrome.storage.session setAccessLevel race. That mechanism does NOT apply here, established by direct measurement, not reasoning.

Instrumentation: timestamped setAccessLevel() call and resolution in background.js; timestamped content-script boot and every loadWorkList() callback with its chrome.runtime.lastError, under counter-suffixed keys so no call overwrote another.

Results across ~30 measurements:
- Isolated: grant ~2ms after SW boot, first loadWorkList ~150ms later.
- 10 parallel copies, idle: sw->granted -643ms to +148ms; granted->first_call 680-1625ms.
- 12 parallel copies under 10-way CPU saturation: sw->granted up to 269ms; granted->first_call 350-2241ms.
- 4 full-suite runs at real concurrency=4: sw->granted -7 to +24ms; granted->first_call 214-284ms.
chrome.runtime.lastError was NEVER non-null at any loadWorkList() call, at any load level, including real full-suite contention.

Why: chip_count_accessibility.test.js's before() calls waitForContentScriptReady() (polls window.__ocToggle) before touching storage.session, which burns enough wall-clock to make the race un-losable.

Also confirmed present on this branch: commit 75d57ba 'drop stale loadWorkList callbacks from torn-down mounts (oculist-3z6)'. That targets a different race and is already merged.

=== LIVE REPRODUCTIONS CAUGHT (3) ===
1. chip_count_accessibility.test.js:214, run 7 of a clean 7-run batch: 'computed accessible name never became "Active search term: unscanned-term", timed out after 5000ms; last observed value: undefined' (5068ms). Did NOT recur across 12 further runs with diagnostics attached.
2. list_search.test.js:357 'removing the only chip in the working list yields activeIndex -1' (29846ms): cdpSession.send Protocol error (Runtime.evaluate): Promise was collected. SAME error class the bead names for chip_row's 'removing the active first chip', and the same shape: a raw Runtime.evaluate({awaitPromise:true}) reading storage.session. 29846ms against a 5000/15000ms budget means the evaluation hung ~30s before CDP gave up, not a slow-but-completing call.
3. find_next_list_ownership CASE 3 timeout, same run as #2.

All three are the same family (carry-over/restored working-list state read via storage.session) but landed on THREE DIFFERENT files, none consistently the ones this bead names. Neither live failure showed a lastError.

=== FLAKE 3, box_sizing_defense: NOT REPRODUCED, two hypotheses DISPROVEN ===
a) WAAPI-vs-wall-clock desync: cyberVisionBracketsSettled is flipped by a raw setTimeout(BRACKET_DELAY + BRACKET_DUR*0.3), not a real completion check. Captured getComputedStyle(bracket).transform for all 4 brackets at the flip instant: matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0) fully settled in 39/39 observations (2 baseline, 18 under 10-way load, 20 under 27-way load). Zero partial transforms.
b) Fire-time vs measure-time drift: snapshotted rect/scrollX/scrollY at beacon fire and at final measurement. Drift exactly 0.0 in all 24 measurements under 27-way saturation.

WORTH RECORDING: the reported 22px delta exactly matches the animation's own hardcoded initial offset (the corners array uses +/-22 as the pre-snap translate offset in content.js). Consistent with a bracket captured before its snap-in animation progressed at all. Could not be forced with CPU-only synthetic load; may need real GPU/compositor contention from many concurrent Chromium processes.

=== CONFOUND, IMPORTANT FOR ANY FUTURE MEASUREMENT ===
Throughout this investigation the host was saturated by an UNRELATED concurrent workload: another Claude session running 'pnpm test:e2e' for a different project (score-viewer) since 01:10, plus this bead's own synthetic load. Machine load average was 20-27. Every flake number above was gathered under that. The investigating agent's conclusion, which the evidence supports, is that these are generic host-resource exhaustion pushing normal async work past its budget and occasionally disrupting the CDP session, rather than one fixable app-level race.
An orphaned npm test run from this investigation (PID 17484/17514) was left running and has been killed.

=== REMAINING OPTION NEEDS A HUMAN ===
The only untried lever in this bead's own step list is retuning --test-concurrency from 4 to 3 in package.json. That is a build-config change affecting every future run and was deliberately NOT made unattended. It is the decision this bead now waits on. Note the suite has grown ~10 Playwright files since the cap was tuned to 4 (per oculist-li8), so the cap is arguably already stale.

Recommend before deciding: re-measure on an otherwise IDLE machine. None of the numbers above were gathered on one.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
Correction to the investigation notes above, so a phantom is not chased later.

The investigating agent's final detached batch reported run 3 as anomalous: 'tests 172, suites 22, pass 148, fail 0' — a truncated run with no failing assertion, no timeout and no CDP error, which it tentatively attributed to an OOM kill under sustained load.

That was almost certainly ME, not OOM. At 01:33 I killed PIDs 17484 (npm test) and 17514 (node --test) to clean up what I had identified as an orphaned run left over from this investigation. That detached batch was still executing at the time. A SIGTERM to the runner mid-suite produces exactly this signature: partial counts, zero recorded failures, truncated reporter output.

Treat run 3 as an artifact of that cleanup. It is NOT a fourth reproduction and NOT evidence of memory pressure. The other six runs in that batch were 249/249.

The genuine reproductions from this investigation remain the three already documented: chip_count_accessibility:214 (5068ms timeout), list_search.test.js:357 (CDP 'Promise was collected', 29846ms), and find_next_list_ownership CASE 3.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
CLOSING as host contention, on the human's decision 2026-08-31 after a clean idle-machine measurement.

THE MEASUREMENT THE EARLIER INVESTIGATION COULD NOT GET: 10 consecutive full-suite runs on an IDLE machine (load average 2.1 at start, 5.6 at end), all 257 tests / 48 suites / 257 pass / 0 fail / 0 CANCELLED. No flake of any kind fired, including the three signatures this bead tracks.

Why that is decisive rather than just lucky. Every prior reproduction in this bead was gathered while the host was saturated at load average 20-27 by an unrelated concurrent workload (another project's e2e suite) plus the investigation's own synthetic load. The three live failures caught then landed on THREE DIFFERENT files, none consistently the ones this bead names, which is the signature of resource exhaustion rather than a specific race.

What was affirmatively RULED OUT, not merely un-reproduced:
- The oculist-z4s setAccessLevel race: ~30 instrumented measurements across isolated, 10-parallel, 12-parallel-under-CPU-saturation and real full-suite runs. chrome.runtime.lastError was NEVER non-null at any loadWorkList() call. The file's own before() waits on waitForContentScriptReady() first, which burns enough wall-clock to make the race un-losable.
- box_sizing WAAPI-vs-wall-clock desync: 39 observations of bracket transform at the settle flag, 100% fully settled, zero partial.
- box_sizing layout/scroll drift: 24 measurements under 27-way saturation, drift exactly 0.0 every time.

Also relevant: the suite has changed materially since those reproductions. oculist-66m made 16 vacuous assertions real, oculist-z4s fixed two contention flakes at root cause, oculist-ex1 added an access-denial retry, and oculist-viv stopped orphaned rAF loops surviving in detached containers, which had been burning CPU for the remainder of a test file's life.

NOT DONE, and deliberately so: --test-concurrency stays at 4. The human declined the 4->3 retune. No measurement shows 4 failing on an idle machine, and the change would cost wall-clock on every future run to buy headroom against a confound that has been removed. Note for anyone revisiting: the suite has grown ~10 Playwright files since that cap was tuned (oculist-li8), so if contention flakes return on a genuinely idle machine, retuning is the first lever to reach for.

Reopen this bead if any of the three signatures recurs on an unloaded machine, and capture the tee'd suite log at the point of failure.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text:
SCEPTICISM WARRANTED ON THIS BEAD'S CLOSURE. Flagged 2026-08-31.

This bead was closed the same day as 'host contention', on the strength of 10 consecutive clean full-suite runs on an idle machine plus several affirmatively ruled-out hypotheses. oculist-8s5 was closed on the SAME reasoning at the SAME time, and has since REPRODUCED: test/trail_effect.test.js:277 failed twice in nine runs at load ~6, with a real assertion (no .oc-trail-arrow mounted), not a timeout.

The flaw in the shared reasoning: 10 clean runs cannot distinguish 'fixed' from 'fires roughly 1 in 5'. Absence of reproduction is weak evidence for a low-frequency intermittent, and the observed 2-in-9 rate would very plausibly produce a 10-run clean streak by chance.

What still stands for THIS bead, and is worth keeping: the affirmatively ruled-out hypotheses are unaffected by the above, because they were positive measurements rather than absence of failure.
- The oculist-z4s setAccessLevel race: ~30 instrumented measurements, chrome.runtime.lastError never non-null.
- box_sizing WAAPI-vs-wall-clock desync: 39 observations, all fully settled.
- box_sizing layout/scroll drift: 24 measurements, drift exactly 0.0.
Those remain valid negative results.

What does NOT still stand: the conclusion that the three signatures this bead tracks were purely host contention and are now gone. Reopen this bead if chip_count_accessibility, the chip-activation 'Promise was collected', or the box_sizing 22px offset recurs on a lightly-loaded machine, and treat a clean streak as insufficient evidence of a fix next time.

title: Speed Lines lane assertion cannot catch whole-effect mispositioning
description: Found by the oculist-dvt.1 re-reviewer via an adversarial mutation the fix was not designed for. The clear-lane test now pins that the lane brackets the match (window.__ocTest.lastSpeedLinesLaneBounds) and that it attenuates real streaks, which kills every fake-lane mutation. FIX: anchor the assertion outside the implementation, e.g. compare the reported matchY against the target element's own getBoundingClientRect() mapped into container-local coordinates, so the test has an independent source of truth for where the match actually is. title: generateListId collision test can leak a frozen Date.now/Math.random
description: Found by the oculist-l6m.22 reviewer. The collision test at test/list_storage.test.js:329-334 freezes Date.now and Math.random in the content-script context, then restores them only INSIDE the saveList callback. If that callback never fires (a rejected write, a thrown error, a timeout), the frozen clock and RNG leak into every remaining test in the file. Two consequences: (1) later tests in list_storage.test.js could behave nondeterministically after an unrelated failure, making the first failure's cause hard to read; (2) separately, if any unrelated page code consumed Math.random between the freeze and generateListId, the test would go green VACUOUSLY rather than fail - a false-negative path. Not observed across 18+ runs, so this is robustness, not a live defect. FIX: restore the overrides in a finally-style guard that runs whether or not the callback fires, and assert the id actually consumed the frozen values so a vacuous pass surfaces as a failure. DONE: forcing saveList's callback never to fire leaves Date.now and Math.random restored for subsequent tests.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: Closed with the finally-backstopped restore (window.__ocFreezeState + idempotent restore reissued from node-side finally, withTimeout bounding a stuck saveList callback) and two anti-vacuity assertions (id embeds frozen Date.now base36; callCountBeforeSave===0 discriminates pre-generateListId burns). Reviewer-verified by three sabotage runs. Accepted residuals, recorded not fixed: (1) a Math.random burn INSIDE content.js's saveList->readListIndex path (after the snapshot) would still pass vacuously - closable later by counting frozen Date.now calls per attempt; (2) __ocFreezeState is never deleted and an unreachable double-freeze would stash frozen fns as originals; (3) the finally's restore eval is itself unbounded and could mask the original error if it rejected. All judged diminishing-returns for a test-robustness bead.

title: test/dispersion_bloom.test.js:164 has a bare timeout: 250
description: Left over from the oculist-rdx sweep, spotted by the oculist-12f reviewer. Most bare 'timeout: 250' values in test/ are per-attempt sub-polls inside 20-attempt retry loops backed by a following scaled page.waitForSelector, which is why oculist-rdx deliberately left them unscaled. Verify whether the one at test/dispersion_bloom.test.js:164 fits that pattern or is a standalone budget that should derive from POLL_TIMEOUT. DONE: the literal is either routed through the shared constants or carries a comment naming it as an intentional short sub-poll.

title: Bloom full-mode assertions live under a Lite Mode test name
description: Found by the oculist-12f reviewer. The full-mode ring offset-order and offset/end-scale pairing assertions added by oculist-12f sit inside the test titled 'Lite Mode drops the ring count from 3 to 1...' in test/dispersion_bloom.test.js (~line 400), because that test already had the full-mode-vs-lite-mode comparison set up. A full-mode pairing regression therefore reports under a Lite Mode test name, which will mislead whoever reads the failure. Structural and pre-existing - oculist-12f extended the existing test rather than introducing the mismatch. FIX: split the full-mode offset/scale contract into its own test block with an accurate name, reusing the ringHueOffsets()/ringEndScales() helpers. DONE: a full-mode pairing mutation fails a test whose name names full mode.

title: Stale synced settings.effect never self-heals in storage
description: Found by the oculist-7z3 reviewer. The registry guard added at content.js:6074 normalises settings.effect in memory but does not call saveSettings(), so chrome.storage.sync keeps the invalid value (e.g. 'lens' from a device on an old build). Every subsequent onChanged echo therefore re-compares 'lens' !== 'hud', sets changed = true, and triggers a full rebuildSettingsPanelPreservingFocus() - permanent low-grade churn for any user with a stale synced value, until they click an effect option and saveSettings() overwrites it. Consistent with the boot-time guard at content.js:6123, which also does not write back, so this is pre-existing behaviour that oculist-7z3 extended rather than introduced. FIX (if judged worth it): have the guard write the normalised value back, or suppress the redraw when the only changed key was normalised to its prior value. Weigh against the risk of a write loop between two devices disagreeing on the effect set. DONE: a stale stored effect is either repaired in storage once, or demonstrably stops triggering repeat rebuilds.

title: storage.onChanged applies settings.effect with no registry guard
description: Found during the oculist-e9u (Lens removal) review. The chrome.storage.onChanged listener at extension/content.js:6062-6069 iterates SETTINGS_KEYS and does settings[k] = nv[k] unconditionally, including 'effect'. It does NOT re-run the boot-time validity guard at content.js:6122 (if (!effectsRegistry[settings.effect]) settings.effect = 'hud'), which only executes inside the initial chrome.storage.sync.get callback. So a remote or stale sync write naming a removed effect - e.g. 'lens' from a device still on the old build - lands in settings.effect post-boot with nothing normalising it. NOT a functional break: animate()'s own fallback (content.js:2589, effectsRegistry[effectKey] || effectsRegistry.hud) catches it at render time and a working HUD beacon still fires; this is pinned by the oculist-e9u regression test in test/settings_panel.test.js, which drives exactly this path. The visible symptom is cosmetic and confined to the settings panel: the effect picker is makeRadioList (content.js:4062-4103), which marks a row active only on an exact item.value === currentVal match, so an unrecognised value matches nothing and EVERY row renders an empty dot - the panel shows no selection at all while the beacon actually renders HUD. It self-heals as soon as the user clicks any option (saveSettings). FIX: apply the same registry guard in the onChanged path, so settings.effect is normalised wherever it is written, not only at boot. DONE: a post-boot storage change naming an unknown effect leaves settings.effect as 'hud' and the panel shows hud selected.

title: Lens: the 1200px source height cap is covered by no test
description: Inverse of oculist-wwu, found by the same reviewer with the opposite mutation. wwu made animateLens's body/html bail independently provable via a short-body fixture. Running the mutation the other way - deleting BOTH height caps (extension/content.js:1666 and the in-walk 'candRect.height <= 1200' at :1641) while leaving the bail intact - leaves the FULL suite green at 145/145. So the cap is now the unproven guard: nothing anywhere fails if it is removed or broken. FIX: add a fixture where the match's nearest non-inline ancestor is a real element (NOT body) taller than 1200px, so the bail cannot fire and the cap is the only guard in play. Assert the lens falls back to the match's immediate parent rather than cloning the oversized ancestor. DONE: deleting the 1200px cap alone fails a test. RELATED NOTE from the same review: the wwu test's 'lens did not mount' branch passes vacuously if the lens fails to draw for an unrelated reason (finder not focused, Enter swallowed). Not vacuous today - mutation proves it bites - and a contention flake would surface as a false failure rather than a false pass, so this is a robustness note, not a correctness bug.

title: Bloom: nothing asserts ring end scales or DOM order
description: Found during the oculist-4qt review by mutation probe. Reversing BOTH ringHueOffsets and ringEndScales in animateDispersion's full-mode path (so -22 pairs with end scale 24.5 instead of 18) leaves the entire suite GREEN, 4/4. Two blind spots cause it: (1) test/dispersion_bloom.test.js:373 sorts the offsets before comparing, so ring DOM order is invisible to the assertion; (2) assertColorsMatch is documented as order-independent; and (3) nothing anywhere in test/ asserts the end-scale values 18/21/24.5 at all. So the 'three rings at -22/0/+22 with end scales 18/21/24.5, in that order' contract is verified only by reading the code. The Lite Mode case is the exception - its offset-0/scale-21 pairing is structurally guaranteed by the shared centred slice, so it needs no separate pinning. FIX: assert the end scales (readable from each ring's animation keyframes or a data attribute if one is added), and compare offsets in DOM order rather than sorted. DONE: reversing the offset/scale arrays, or mispairing an offset with the wrong end scale, fails a test. SEPARATE MINOR ITEM from the same review: for ringCount > 3 the centred-slice arithmetic yields a negative ringStart, so slice(-1, 3) silently under-renders (ringCount 4 or 5 draws ONE ring, not four). No undefined or NaN, so it is safe, but quietly wrong. Clamp with Math.max(0, ringStart) or add a comment naming the ceiling, if ringCount ever becomes tunable.

title: Lens: the body/html bail and the 1200px source cap mask each other in tests
description: In animateLens (extension/content.js ~1600), two guards stop the effect cloning the whole document: an unconditional bail when the resolved sourceEl is document.body/documentElement, and a ~1200px height cap on the resolved source. In test/lens_effect.test.js the fixture body is ~2000px tall, so removing the bail alone still leaves the suite green (the height cap catches it instead); only removing BOTH turns it red. The assertion is not vacuous, but the bail is not independently mutation-provable. FIX: add a fixture page with a SHORT body (under 1200px) carrying a bare text-node match directly under <body>, so the bail is the only guard in play and removing it goes red on its own. Found by the reviewer on oculist-y6a, ruled non-blocking. DONE: removing the body/html bail alone fails a test.

title: Dispersion Bloom's Lite Mode ring uses the -22 hue offset, not the base palette hue
description: In animateDispersion (extension/content.js:1381-1383), the ring loop indexes hueOffsets by r. With ringCount = 1 under Lite Mode (settings.performanceMode), the single rendered ring therefore takes hueOffsets[0] === -22 rather than the base 0 offset — so Lite Mode users see the beacon shifted 22 degrees off getEffectiveColors().beacon instead of the palette colour itself. Still palette-derived and still colourblind-safe, so this is cosmetic, not an accessibility defect. FIX: when ringCount === 1, emit the 0 offset (e.g. pick the middle of the offsets array, or slice the offsets to a centred subset sized to ringCount). Also add a length guard so endScales/hueOffsets indexing cannot silently yield undefined/NaN colours if ringCount ever grows past the array length — safe today only because it is always 1 or 3. Found by the reviewer on oculist-dvv, ruled non-blocking. DONE: Lite Mode renders one ring at the unshifted palette beacon hue, and a test pins it.

title: renameList silently discards a malformed terms value with no user notice
description: Found during oculist-dzi review. renameList (content.js:386) does terms: Array.isArray(existing.terms) ? existing.terms : [], so renaming an entry whose terms is malformed silently replaces it with an empty array. The user gets no notice that data was discarded. This path was unreachable before oculist-dzi, because malformed entries were invisible in the panel and so had no reachable rename button; dzi made them visible and deletable, which also made this the one user-reachable lossy path it opened up. dzi corrected the comment at content.js:363-366 so the behaviour is at least documented, which was the actual ask there, but the silence to the user remains. Normalising garbage on an explicit user write is defensible and matches the 0-terms badge the panel already shows, so this is low priority. Options: leave as-is now that it is documented; surface a notice via showNotice with its own key (the per-class notice machinery from oculist-l6m.12 makes this cheap); or preserve the unknown value so a user could recover it. Done: renaming an entry with malformed terms either tells the user the value was discarded, or preserves it.

title: traverse()'s text-node branch still duplicates isOculistNode() with an ad-hoc oc-beacon check
description: Found during oculist-l6m.14 review. content.js:2248 (the text-node branch of traverse()) still uses an ad-hoc parent.classList.contains('oc-beacon') instead of routing through isOculistNode(), which is the last remaining duplicate of that helper inside traverse() after l6m.14 fixed the element branch. It is currently dead defense rather than a live gap: any Oculist ancestor is now rejected before descent, so the text-node branch can no longer be reached for Oculist-owned text. Worth collapsing for the same reason l6m.14 existed - the duplicate will silently diverge from isOculistNode() if the helper gains a new marker. Done: the text-node branch routes through isOculistNode(), or carries a comment saying why it deliberately does not.

title: X-button chip removal briefly shows the removed term's count and highlights for one debounce tick
description: Found during oculist-l6m.33 review, verified with a live probe. Removing the only chip via the X button while a search debounce is still in flight (<150ms) shows the removed term's stale count and highlights for one debounce tick, then self-heals to the draft's correct state. Transient, self-limiting, and internally consistent throughout - the count, nav state and highlights agree with each other at every instant, they are just briefly the removed term's. Not a done-criteria failure for .33; filed as polish. Fix would be to cancel or invalidate the in-flight debounce on X-button removal the way the Backspace path already resets lastTerm (content.js removeChipAt, ~line 3003).

title: Whitespace-only stored terms render an enabled load control that does nothing
description:
Found during oculist-l6m.26 review. Corrupted or hand-edited storage only, non-destructive.

Three gates disagree about what counts as an empty term list:
- buildListItem (content.js:3753) gates on raw list.terms.length
- loadSavedList (content.js:3682) gates on sanitizeListTerms(...).length
- listSavedLists (content.js:250) filters to strings without trimming

So a stored list with terms: ['   '] renders an ENABLED load control badged "1 term", and
clicking it is a silent no-op, because loadSavedList sanitizes the whitespace away and hits
its empty early-return.

Not reachable by saving through the UI, since saveList now rejects empty-after-sanitize.
Reachable via hand-edited or corrupted sync storage.

Done: the three gates agree on one definition of empty, applied consistently.

title: Dead assertion and missing dedupe defence from .6
description:
Two one-liners found during oculist-l6m.6 review.

1. test/dim_highlight.test.js:204 asserts priorities.dim === 0, but 0 is the CSS spec default
   for Highlight.priority, so deleting the assignment at content.js:1977 can never fail it.
   The assertion cannot detect what it appears to test.
2. normalizeWorkList (content.js:102-109) does not dedupe terms. updateDimHighlight skips the
   active term BY INDEX, not by text, so a session payload with a repeated term would put the
   active term's own ranges into the dim set. Unreachable through the UI today because
   addChipTerm dedupes on add.

Done: the assertion tests something real or is removed with a comment saying why; normalizeWorkList dedupes.
notes:
THIRD ONE-LINER from the .5 review: the else branch inside the committed-Enter block (content.js:2833-2836) is unreachable, because performListSearch() always sets firstEnter = true when searchRanges.length > 0. Remove it or explain why it stays.
FOURTH ONE-LINER from the .7 review: the Lite Mode toggle rescan (content.js:4232) fires even when the bar is closed and wrap is null, paying a full buildPageIndex() for no visible effect. Guard on wrap.
FIFTH ONE-LINER, from the .19 re-review: content.js:2680-2689 nests if (!hasActiveChip) inside if (!term) where if (!term && !hasActiveChip) reads better. Cosmetic only.
SIXTH ONE-LINER, from the .27 review: .oc-settings-reset-btn's accessible name is the literal string '↺ Reset', so the glyph leaks into what a screen reader announces. Move the glyph out of the accessible name.

comments.author: ya8282
comments.text: All six one-liners landed and review-passed. Notes: (1) dim priority assertion removed with mutation evidence (0 is the spec default, deletion undetectable); (2) normalizeWorkList dedupes exact-string keep-first with activeIndex remap - known pre-existing divergence: addChipTerm trims before comparing, normalizeWorkList does not, so a crafted payload ['a',' a'] still yields two chips (unreachable via UI); (3) unreachable else independently re-verified and removed; (4) lite-mode rescan guarded on wrap - guard is defensively redundant since __ocDestroy clears workListTerms; (6) reset glyph now aria-hidden - cosmetic risk noted by reviewer: inline-flex may collapse the glyph span's trailing space so the visual gap between the glyph and 'Reset' could shrink; untested, fix with gap/margin if it looks wrong.
